description: Organization-wide Renovate policy for liverty-music, inherited by every repository in the org.

Renovate auto-discovers this file in the org's .github repository, so a policy change here takes effect everywhere without editing each repository. Per-repository renovate.json files add only what is specific to their stack.

Built by extending config:best-practices rather than assembling rules by hand: a locally copied group does not learn about packages added upstream later, so it narrows silently while continuing to look correct. See the OpenSpec change `automate-dependency-updates`, design D14.

The recurring human actions this policy implies — regenerating visual baselines after a Playwright bump, reviewing a Pulumi preview, handling an urgent fix held by the release-age delay, updating buf.lock by hand — are documented in renovate-runbook.md next to this file.

The observation cycle this schedule was briefly lifted for is complete. It corrected four assumptions that could only be checked by running Renovate: `group:pulumi` does NOT group the Pulumi providers (they are grouped locally now, as noise reduction — they are not version-coupled); BSR-generated Go modules cannot be looked up at all; our own container images were being proposed for update, which would have been a deployment; and `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests` was pinning our OWN reusable workflow, severing the `@main` reference it depends on. What the cycle CONFIRMED: `group:monorepos` works for Vitest, OpenTelemetry JS and the Node family (`node` + `@types/node` in one pull request), the Playwright custom manager matches all three of its locations, and Aurelia stays on `2.0.0-rc.2` without a local rule — so none was written.

packageRules.description: Release-age delay, stated explicitly so it survives a schedule change. config:best-practices brings security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm, which covers npm only; these are the other datasources this org automerges, and each is equally reachable by a compromised maintainer account. NOTE: this delay is NOT bypassed for vulnerability fixes. Renovate's vulnerability path ignores schedule and the concurrency limits, but not minimumReleaseAge. That is deliberate and left as-is: a delay exists precisely because a release claiming to be a security fix can itself be the attack. A genuinely urgent fix is merged by hand — see the runbook.
Monthly cadence for the slow-moving, high-fan-out axes. Weekly proposals for these produce churn out of proportion to how often they actually matter.
schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Keep @biomejs/biome on one cadence across the org. frontend and cloud-provisioning pin it to the same exact version, and Renovate cannot group across repositories — so the two will always be two pull requests. Putting the schedule here rather than in each repository's config is what keeps them landing close together: a per-repo schedule change could silently desynchronise the formatter, and a formatter mismatch rewrites files on every save.

Do NOT pin liverty-music's own Actions and reusable workflows to a SHA. `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests` (from config:best-practices) pins every `uses:` reference it finds, and it caught `liverty-music/.github/.github/workflows/claude-review.yml@main` in all three repositories that consume it. That reference is `@main` deliberately: the whole point of a reusable workflow is that fixing it in one place reaches every consumer, and freezing it to a SHA severs exactly that. The security argument for pinning does not apply either — pinning protects against a third party repointing a tag at code we have not read, and this is our own code under our own review. The capability states the exemption directly: "Actions published from within the liverty-music organization are exempt, as their contents are already under this project's control."

STAGE 1 AUTOMERGE — the lowest-risk axes. `automerge` stays false at the top level and is turned on here per group, rather than flipped on globally with exclusions: with exclusions, forgetting one means it merges, and the failure is silent. This way forgetting one means it waits for a person. Restricted to minor/patch/digest. Majors never automerge (the capability forbids it), and `pin` is left out deliberately — pin pull requests interact oddly with the release-age check (Renovate does not wire release age into pin, renovatebot/renovate#40288), and that interaction has not been observed under automerge yet.

STAGE 1 AUTOMERGE — npm devDependencies. Build and test tooling: a break shows up as a red pipeline on the next pull request rather than in production. Note the repository-level exclusions still win over this, because a repository's own `renovate.json` rules are evaluated after the inherited preset — `@playwright/test` is a devDependency and stays excluded in frontend, because a bump invalidates committed visual baselines that Renovate cannot regenerate.

STAGE 2 (task 10.4) — runtime npm dependencies, minor and patch. Stage 1 enabled `devDependencies`; this is the same decision extended to `dependencies`, which is where the Aurelia runtime packages, the OpenTelemetry JS family, `workbox-background-sync` and the Connect-RPC web client live. The evidence is the same evidence: these repositories gate merges on `CI Success`, which runs lint, typecheck, unit tests, the Storybook component tests against committed visual baselines, and the Playwright E2E and PWA projects. Major updates are NOT listed and therefore still inherit the global `automerge: false`. Two packages are deliberately left out and their exclusions live in `frontend/renovate.json` and `cloud-provisioning/renovate.json`, not here, because the reasons are repository-specific: `@playwright/test` invalidates committed screenshot baselines that Renovate cannot regenerate, `vite-plugin-pwa` has an install-prompt surface CI cannot reach, npm `overrides` encode a judgement whose correct resolution is often removal, and a Pulumi provider cannot be judged without a preview run against production credentials. A repository's own rules are merged AFTER this preset's and later matches win, so each of those exclusions overrides this rule.

STAGE 2 (task 10.4) — Go modules, minor and patch. Covers the OpenTelemetry Go and Connect-RPC Go modules, `stripe-go`, the `zitadel/*` and `pannpers/*` libraries, and the `go-tools` group of build CLIs. `backend` runs `go build`, `go test` and `golangci-lint` behind `CI Success`, with `postUpdateOptions: [gomodTidy]` so the module graph is settled in the same commit. The BSR-generated modules cannot reach this rule: `buf.build/gen/go/**` is `enabled: false` in `backend/renovate.json` — `liverty-music/schema/*` by policy, because it advances with the OpenSpec change and its code migration, and `pocketsign/apis/*` because Renovate cannot resolve its version format at all. Task 10.4 lists the pocketsign SDK as a family to enable; it is not enabled and cannot be, and the manual bump in the runbook remains its only path.

The Go version itself is patch-only (task 10.5), so `1.27.1 -> 1.27.2` merges unattended and `1.27 -> 1.28` waits for a person. This is not caution about Renovate — it is Go's numbering. A Go `1.N` release is a language release with a new compiler, garbage collector and standard library, which every other ecosystem would call a major; only the third component is a patch release. Renovate classifies it as `minor`, so the general gomod rule above would automerge it. This rule is placed after that one and wins. It matches on the `golang-version` datasource rather than on the name `go`, because that is what actually identifies the Go release: the gomod manager emits both the `go` and the `toolchain` directive as `depName: "go"` with `datasource: "golang-version"`, and matching the datasource cannot be confused with a Go module that happens to be named `go`. The other Go declarations are unaffected and are meant to be: `golang:1.27-alpine` is a Docker tag at major.minor precision that a patch release does not move, and `.golangci.yml` no longer pins a version at all — it reads `go.mod`. Node needs no equivalent rule: `.nvmrc` holds `22`, `engines.node` is a range and `node:22-alpine` is a major.minor tag, so none of them receives a patch update; the only Node dependency at full precision is `@types/node`, a devDependency already covered by stage 1.

PERMANENT: the .github repository never automerges. It has no GitHubRepositoryComponent in cloud-provisioning, so it has no branch protection, no required status checks and no CI of its own — an automerge there would land with no gate whatsoever, which is the opposite of the policy this configuration implements. Renovate still raises pull requests for its GitHub Actions; a human merges them. Removing this rule requires first giving .github its own CI and protection (design D11, follow-up 12.4).
